methodAuthority.paper: Guo, Sang, Tu & Wang (2024), Cross-cryptocurrency return predictability, Journal of Economic Dynamics and Control 163, 104863
sourceFacts: Minute-frequency Binance returns exhibit cross-cryptocurrency predictability up to ten minutes without reversal.
BTC is a leading positive predictor for other non-stable cryptocurrencies.
The paper forms equal-weight quintiles on out-of-sample forecasts and reports positive futures long-short performance after taker costs with ten-minute rebalancing.
methodAuthority.adaptation: Frozen univariate BTC lead-lag replication screen on Binance USD-M perpetuals; not an exact reconstruction of the paper's full adaptive-LASSO model.
methodAuthority.estimator: Per-target OLS with intercept: target 1m return at s on BTC 1m return at s-1, using the prior 720 completed training pairs only.
methodAuthority.forecast: At decision minute t after its close, forecast target minute t+1 using the fitted intercept/beta and completed BTC return at t.
methodAuthority.holding: Enter at next 1m open and hold ten minutes to the open ten minutes later.
methodAuthority.portfolio: Equal-weight long highest forecast quintile +0.50, short lowest forecast quintile -0.50; BTC is predictor only and is not a target.

dataAuthority.transportRule: Missing/corrupt decisions fail closed; no interpolation or forward fill.

universe.selection: Prelocked established USD-M contracts chosen only from already-used causally-distinct project universes before ARP30 price outcomes; no post-outcome substitution.

costs.chargedOn: sum absolute long/short portfolio weight changes plus terminal liquidation
costs.funding: Development is a price-alpha screen. Exact Binance funding cashflow replay under unchanged signals is mandatory before validation authorization.

statistics.decisionReturnAggregation: Compound ten-minute portfolio returns within UTC day, then evaluate daily series.

failureRule: Any development gate failure closes ARP30-XCR1 with no cadence, universe, training-window, direction, cost, liquidity, estimator, or gate rescue. A development pass does not open validation: exact funding cashflows must first be replayed under identical frozen signals. Validation failure keeps holdout sealed. R15 remains untouched until all final release gates pass.
